newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business group hails Republican Congress.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business group hails Republican Congress.

text.p: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce hailed the Republican victory in both houses of Congress on Wednesday, saying it would provide a pro-business counter-balance to the Clinton administration.

"Clearly this was a watershed election for American business and this Congress will be there to offset the excesses of the second Clinton administration," said Frank Coleman, vice president of the business group.
Republicans recaptured both the House and Senate, marking the first time the party has controlled both chambers for consecutive sessions since before the Second World War.
Coleman also said the Republican victory showed the AFL-CIO's campaign strategy had "backfired."
The AFL-CIO spent about $35 million on the campaign, including $25 million on "issue oriented" attack ads. A coalition of business groups spent $5 million on counter ads.
"They hurt their own credibility with outright lies and the public responded when it was made clear these ads were filled with falsehoods," Coleman said.
